new_note: *And they kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days, making merry before Yahuah (God),* (1 Esdras 7:14). *Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Messiah (Christ) our passover is sacrificed for us:* (1 Corinthians 5:7). The exiles had come up out of Babylon, and the first thing they did after the Passover was keep the seven days of unleavened bread, glad before Yahuah (God). Paul writes to an assembly far from Jerusalem and tells them to purge out the old leaven for the same reason, because Messiah (Christ) our Passover has been slain, and the next line says it plainly, let us keep the feast. The lamb being slain did not end the feast; it is the reason the feast is kept. The returned remnant and the assembly at Corinth are keeping the same appointed days, and the one the days point to is Yahusha (Jesus).
member_note: 1 Esdras 7:14 — *they kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days, making merry before Yahuah (God).* Messiah (Christ) our Passover is the reason the feast is kept, not the end of it (1 Corinthians 5:7).

new_note: *For both they and their sons have married with their daughters, and the holy seed is mixed with the strange people of the land; and from the beginning of this matter the rulers and the great men have been partakers of this iniquity.* (1 Esdras 8:70). *But yet in it shall be a tenth, and it shall return, and shall be eaten: as a teil tree, and as an oak, whose substance is in them, when they cast their leaves: so the holy seed shall be the substance thereof.* (Isaiah 6:13). Both verses call the people the holy seed, and both mean a bloodline. Esdras rends his garment because the seed of Yashar'el (Israel) has been mixed with the strange people of the land, and the rulers led the way in it. Isaiah had already said what would become of that seed: the tree is cut down to a stump, a tenth returns, and the holy seed is what remains alive in the stump when everything else is eaten away. The grief in Esdras and the promise in Isaiah are about the same seed, and the promise is that Yahuah (God) keeps it through the cutting.
member_note: 1 Esdras 8:70 — *the holy seed is mixed with the strange people of the land.* Isaiah 6:13 names the same holy seed as what remains alive in the stump.
flag: The word 'substance' in this card is inside the verbatim KJV text of Isaiah 6:13, not in the note's prose; left as the source reads.

new_note: *O Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), you are true: for we are left a root this day.* (1 Esdras 8:89). *O Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), thou art righteous: for we remain yet escaped, as it is this day: behold, we are before thee in our trespasses: for we cannot stand before thee because of this.* (Ezra 9:15). These are the same prayer told twice, once by Ezra and once by Esdras. In both, the man kneels with torn garments and confesses that Yahuah (God) is righteous and the people are not, that they are a root left this day, a remnant yet escaped, and that they cannot stand before him because of what they have done. The confession does not plead the people's merit; it pleads his faithfulness, you are true. A root left and a remnant escaped is how Yahuah (God) keeps his word to the fathers when the sons have broken theirs.
member_note: 1 Esdras 8:89 — *you are true: for we are left a root this day.* Ezra 9:15 is the same confession: he is righteous, and a remnant yet escaped.

new_note: *And that whoever met not there within two or three days according as the elders that bare rule appointed, their cattle should be seized to the use of the temple, and himself cast out from them that were of the captivity.* (1 Esdras 9:4). *And that whosoever would not come within three days, according to the counsel of the princes and the elders, all his substance should be forfeited, and himself separated from the congregation of those that had been carried away.* (Ezra 10:8). Ezra and 1 Esdras record the same proclamation. Everyone of the captivity was to gather at Jerusalem within three days, and whoever stayed away forfeited his goods and was cut off from the congregation of the returned. The matter was the strange wives, and the remedy began with the whole remnant standing together in one place before anything was decided. The two accounts agree on the terms, the goods seized for the temple and the man put out, so the reader can watch one event through two witnesses.
member_note: 1 Esdras 9:4 — *their cattle should be seized to the use of the temple, and himself cast out.* Ezra 10:8 records the same three-day summons and the same forfeit.
flag: The word 'substance' in this card is inside the verbatim KJV text of Ezra 10:8, not in the note's prose; left as the source reads.

new_note: *Wherefore they chose rather to die, that they might not be defiled with meats, and that they might not profane the holy covenant: so then they died.* (1 Maccabees 1:63). *For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.* (Matthew 26:28). Under Antiochus the faithful in Yashar'el (Israel) chose death over unclean meat because eating it would profane the holy covenant, and so they died. At the table Yahusha (Jesus) names his own blood the blood of the new covenant, shed for many. The covenant the Maccabean faithful died for and the covenant he died to seal are not two covenants with two laws; Jeremiah says the new covenant is the law written in the inward parts and on the heart, the same law those men would not break. They gave their lives rather than profane it; he gave his to write it where it could not be taken from them.
member_note: 1 Maccabees 1:63 — *that they might not profane the holy covenant: so then they died.* The blood of the new covenant (Matthew 26:28) seals the same covenant they died for.

new_note: *Wherefore they chose rather to die, that they might not be defiled with meats, and that they might not profane the holy covenant: so then they died.* (1 Maccabees 1:63). *But said, Let us die all in our innocency: heaven and earth will testify for us, that you put us to death wrongfully.* (1 Maccabees 2:37). The two verses sit a chapter apart and describe the same resolve. In chapter 1 the faithful choose death over defilement so the holy covenant is not profaned. In chapter 2 a company hiding in the wilderness is attacked on the sabbath and answers, let us die all in our innocency, and calls heaven and earth to witness that they are being killed wrongfully. Neither group bargained with the covenant to buy a day of life. Their deaths are the measure of what the law of Yahuah (God) was worth to them, and the book records them so the reader will know what the covenant cost before the Maccabees ever drew a sword.
member_note: 1 Maccabees 1:63 — *they chose rather to die, that they might not be defiled with meats.* The same resolve as those who said let us die all in our innocency (1 Maccabees 2:37).

new_note: *At that time therefore they decreed, saying, Whoever shall come to make battle with us on the sabbath day, we will fight against him; neither will we die all, as our brothers that were murdered in the secret places.* (1 Maccabees 2:41). *How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.* (Matthew 12:12). After a thousand of their brothers were slaughtered in the caves rather than lift a hand on the sabbath, Mattathias and his men decreed that they would fight whoever came against them on that day. They were not setting the sabbath aside; they were refusing to let the heathen use the sabbath to root the people who kept it out of the earth. Yahusha (Jesus) makes the same judgment when he asks whether a man is worth more than a sheep pulled from a pit on the sabbath and answers that it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days. The sabbath was given for life; to preserve life on it is to keep it, not to break it.
member_note: 1 Maccabees 2:41 — *Whoever shall come to make battle with us on the sabbath day, we will fight against him.* Preserving life on the sabbath is doing well on it (Matthew 12:12).

new_note: *Now therefore, my sons, be you zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.* (1 Maccabees 2:50). *For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.* (Matthew 26:28). Mattathias, dying, charges his sons to be zealous for the law and to give their lives for the covenant of their fathers. The King does both. His zeal for his Father's house and his Father's commandments runs through the gospels, and at the table he gives his life, his blood of the new covenant shed for many. The covenant of the fathers and the new covenant are one covenant; what is new in Jeremiah 31 is where the law is written, on the heart, not whether it stands. So the zeal Mattathias asked of his sons is not a different thing from what Yahusha (Jesus) poured out; it is the same love of the same law, carried to the same end.
member_note: 1 Maccabees 2:50 — *be you zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.* The King gave his life for that covenant; his blood of the new covenant is shed for many (Matthew 26:28).

new_note: *Now therefore, my sons, be you zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.* (1 Maccabees 2:50). *And he said unto them, This is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many.* (Mark 14:24). A dying father tells his sons to give their lives for the covenant of their fathers, and the sons do it, one after another, through the rest of the book. Mark records the King doing the same thing with his own blood, the blood of the new covenant, shed for many. The many he died for are the people whose fathers cut that covenant at Sinai and whose sons died for it under Antiochus. Mattathias asked his sons for what Yahusha (Jesus) gave, and the covenant both were given for is the same covenant, now written on the heart.
member_note: 1 Maccabees 2:50 — *give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.* Mark 14:24, the King's blood of the new covenant shed for many, is a life given for that covenant.

new_note: *Elias for being zealous and fervent for the law was taken up into heaven.* (1 Maccabees 2:58). *And if ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.* (Matthew 11:14). Mattathias remembers Elijah (Elias) for one thing: he was zealous and fervent for the law, and he was taken up into heaven. That is how the faithful in Yashar'el (Israel) remembered him, as the man who stood for the commandments of Yahuah (God) against a kingdom that had traded them for Baal. When Yahusha (Jesus) says of John, this is Elijah (Elias) which was for to come, the likeness is that same zeal: John in the wilderness calling the leadership a generation of vipers, John in prison for telling Herod his marriage was unlawful. Elijah's zeal for the law is what Malachi promised would come before the great day, and it came first in John.
member_note: 1 Maccabees 2:58 — *Elias for being zealous and fervent for the law was taken up into heaven.* John came in that same zeal; this is Elias which was for to come (Matthew 11:14).

new_note: *Then said Judas and his brothers, Behold, our enemies are discomfited: let us go up to cleanse and dedicate the sanctuary.* (1 Maccabees 4:36). *And said unto them that sold doves, Take these things hence; make not my Father’s house an house of merchandise.* (John 2:16). Judas and his brothers, with the enemy beaten back, go up to cleanse and dedicate the sanctuary the heathen had defiled. Generations later Yahusha (Jesus) walks into the same house and drives out the sellers, saying make not my Father's house an house of merchandise. The Maccabees cleansed what Antiochus had polluted with his idol; the King cleansed what the priests had polluted with their market. It is the same motion, the house of Yahuah (God) purged of what does not belong in it, and the second time it is done by the Son whose Father's house it is.
member_note: 1 Maccabees 4:36 — *let us go up to cleanse and dedicate the sanctuary.* The King cleansed the same house: make not my Father's house an house of merchandise (John 2:16).

new_note: *Who cleansed the sanctuary, and bare out the defiled stones into an unclean place.* (1 Maccabees 4:43). *And Yahusha (Jesus) went into the temple of Elohim (God), and cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves,* (Matthew 21:12). The priests Judas chose carried the defiled stones out of the sanctuary to an unclean place. Yahusha (Jesus) went into the temple of Elohim (God) and carried out the sellers, the buyers, the tables, and the seats. What defiled the house in Judas's day was an idol the Greeks had set on the altar; what defiled it in the King's day was trade the priesthood had set in the court of prayer. Both were put out. Cleansing the sanctuary is what faithful men do when the house of Yahuah (God) has been made to serve something other than him.
member_note: 1 Maccabees 4:43 — *cleansed the sanctuary, and bare out the defiled stones into an unclean place.* The King cast out what defiled the same house (Matthew 21:12).

new_note: *And laid up the stones in the mountain of the temple in a convenient place, until there should come a prophet to shew what should be done with them.* (1 Maccabees 4:46). *And said unto them, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.* (Matthew 21:13). Judas's priests did not know what to do with the stones of the profaned altar, so they laid them up on the temple mount until a prophet should come to say. Yahusha (Jesus) came into that temple as the prophet the crowds had just named him, the prophet of Nazareth (Matthew 21:11), and the word he gave about the house was from the prophets already written: it is written, my house shall be called the house of prayer. The Maccabees waited for a prophet to tell them what the house required. When he came, he told them, and what it required was that it be a house of prayer and not a den of thieves.
member_note: 1 Maccabees 4:46 — *until there should come a prophet to shew what should be done with them.* The prophet came and spoke for the house: my house shall be called the house of prayer (Matthew 21:13).

new_note: *Yet at the last, their vessels being without victuals, (for that it was the seventh year, and they in Judea that were delivered from the Gentiles, had eaten up the residue of the store;) There were but a few left in the sanctuary, because the famine did so prevail against them, that they were fain to disperse themselves, every man to his own place.* (1 Maccabees 6:53–54). *But the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie still; that the poor of thy people may eat: and what they leave the beasts of the field shall eat. In like manner thou shalt deal with thy vineyard, and with thy oliveyard.* (Exodus 23:11). The defenders in the sanctuary were not broken for want of courage but for want of bread, and the book says why: it was the seventh year, and the land had rested. Exodus commands that in the seventh year the land lie still so the poor may eat, and the people of Judea had kept it even with an army at the gates. The handful left in the sanctuary dispersed because there was nothing in the storehouse, and there was nothing in the storehouse because they had obeyed Yahuah (God). The book records the cost without apology, because the sabbath of the land was his commandment and they kept it.
member_note: 1 Maccabees 6:54 — *There were but a few left in the sanctuary, because the famine did so prevail against them.* The famine came because they kept the seventh-year rest of Exodus 23:11.

new_note: *And to intreat them that they would take the yoke from them; for they saw that the kingdom of the Grecians did oppress Yashar'el (Israel) with servitude.* (1 Maccabees 8:18). *Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong; but they look not unto the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel), neither seek Yahuah (LORD)!* (Isaiah 31:1). Judas sent to Rome asking them to take the Greek yoke off Yashar'el (Israel). Isaiah had pronounced woe on those who go down to Egypt for help and trust in horses and chariots because they are many, instead of looking to the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel). Rome was many and very strong, and the league was made, and in time the yoke of Rome lay heavier on the land than the yoke of the Greeks ever had. The verse in 1 Maccabees does not condemn the embassy, but Isaiah does, and the reader who has both in front of him can see what the arm of flesh bought.
member_note: 1 Maccabees 8:18 — *to intreat them that they would take the yoke from them.* The embassy to Rome is the going down to Egypt for help that Isaiah 31:1 warns against.

new_note: *For every man sat under his vine and his fig tree, and there was none to fray them:* (1 Maccabees 14:12). *In that day, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), shall ye call every man his neighbour under the vine and under the fig tree.* (Zechariah 3:10). Under Simon the land had peace, and every man sat under his vine and his fig tree with no one to frighten him. Zechariah uses the same picture, but he fixes it to a day, in that day, and the verses before it name whose day it is: the BRANCH, the servant Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) will bring forth. Simon's peace lasted a few years and ended in blood at a banquet. The vine and the fig tree in 1 Maccabees 14 are a foretaste the people were given; the vine and the fig tree in Zechariah 3 are the rest the Messiah (Christ) brings, which no one will take away.
member_note: 1 Maccabees 14:12 — *every man sat under his vine and his fig tree, and there was none to fray them.* A foretaste of the day of the BRANCH in Zechariah 3:10.

new_note: *Then had I pity upon your mournings, and gave you manna to eat; so you did eat angels’ bread.* (2 Esdras 1:19). *When Yahusha (Jesus) heard of it, he departed thence by ship into a desert place apart: and when the people had heard thereof, they followed him on foot out of the cities.* (Matthew 14:13). In 2 Esdras Yahuah (God) reminds the people that when they murmured in the wilderness he pitied them and fed them with manna, angels' bread. In Matthew the King goes by ship into a desert place and the people follow on foot out of the cities, and the verses that follow say he was moved with compassion and fed them there. The same pity, the same wilderness, the same bread given to a multitude that had nothing. The one who fed the fathers by the hand of Moses fed the children with his own hands by the sea of Galilee.
member_note: 2 Esdras 1:19 — *Then had I pity upon your mournings, and gave you manna to eat.* The same pity fed the multitude in the desert place of Matthew 14:13.

new_note: *Then had I pity upon your mournings, and gave you manna to eat; so you did eat angels’ bread.* (2 Esdras 1:19). *For the bread of Elohim (God) is he which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life unto the world.* (John 6:33). The manna was angels' bread, 2 Esdras says, given out of the Father's pity. In John, Yahusha (Jesus) tells the crowd that the bread of Elohim (God) is he which comes down from heaven and gives life to the world, and a few verses on he says it outright, I am the bread of life. The fathers ate angels' bread in the wilderness and died; the bread the Father sends now is a person, and the life he gives does not end at the edge of the wilderness. The manna was real bread and a real sign, and the one it signified stood in the synagogue at Capernaum and said so.
member_note: 2 Esdras 1:19 — *so you did eat angels’ bread.* The bread of Elohim (God) that comes down from heaven is the one the manna pointed to (John 6:33).

new_note: *I gathered you together, as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings: but now, what shall I do to you? I will cast you out from my face.* (2 Esdras 1:30). *O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!* (Matthew 23:37). The voice in 2 Esdras is Yahuah (God) speaking to Yashar'el (Israel): I gathered you as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings, and you would not stay gathered. In the temple Yahusha (Jesus) says the same words over Jerusalem in the first person, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not. He is not borrowing a figure of speech; he is the one who did the gathering the figure describes, the one who spoke to the fathers and now stands in the city that killed the prophets he sent. The hen is the same hen, the children are the same children, and the refusal is the same refusal.
member_note: 2 Esdras 1:30 — *I gathered you together, as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings.* The King speaks the same words in the same voice over Jerusalem (Matthew 23:37).

new_note: *I sent to you my servants the prophets, whom you have taken and slain, and torn their bodies in pieces, whose blood I will require of your hands, says Yahuah (God).* (2 Esdras 1:32). *And the husbandmen took his servants, and beat one, and killed another, and stoned another.* (Matthew 21:35). Yahuah (God) says he sent his servants the prophets and the people took them, slew them, and tore their bodies in pieces, and he will require their blood. In the parable the husbandmen take the owner's servants and beat one, kill another, and stone another. The servants are the prophets, the husbandmen are the men set over the vineyard, and the owner who sent them is going to require the blood. The parable is not a new story; the King is telling the leadership of his day the history already written against their fathers, and daring them to finish it.
member_note: 2 Esdras 1:32 — *I sent to you my servants the prophets, whom you have taken and slain.* The husbandmen who beat, killed, and stoned the servants (Matthew 21:35) are the same story.

new_note: *I sent to you my servants the prophets, whom you have taken and slain, and torn their bodies in pieces, whose blood I will require of your hands, says Yahuah (God).* (2 Esdras 1:32). *Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city:* (Matthew 23:34). The pattern in 2 Esdras is past tense: I sent my servants the prophets, you slew them, I will require their blood. In Matthew 23 the King turns it to the future: behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes, and some of them ye shall kill. He is the sender in both. The same voice that sent Jeremiah and Zechariah to be rejected now sends apostles to be scourged in the synagogues and chased from city to city, and the next verses say the blood of all of them, from Abel onward, will be required of that generation. What Yahuah (God) promised through Esdras, Yahusha (Jesus) pronounces in the temple.
member_note: 2 Esdras 1:32 — *whose blood I will require of your hands, says Yahuah (God).* The same sender says, behold, I send unto you prophets, and some of them ye shall kill (Matthew 23:34).

new_note: *Thus says the Almighty Yahuah (God), Your house is desolate, I will cast you out as the wind does stubble.* (2 Esdras 1:33). *And they caught him, and cast him out of the vineyard, and slew him.* (Matthew 21:39). The sentence in 2 Esdras follows directly on the slaying of the prophets: your house is desolate, I will cast you out as the wind does stubble. The parable follows the same order. After the servants are beaten and killed the son is sent, and the husbandmen cast him out of the vineyard and slay him, and the King asks his hearers what the owner will do to them. The desolate house is the answer. Killing the prophets brought the sentence near; killing the son brought it down, and within a generation not one stone of that house was left on another.
member_note: 2 Esdras 1:33 — *Your house is desolate, I will cast you out as the wind does stubble.* The sentence falls when the husbandmen cast out the son and slay him (Matthew 21:39).

new_note: *Thus says the Almighty Yahuah (God), Your house is desolate, I will cast you out as the wind does stubble.* (2 Esdras 1:33). *Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.* (Matthew 23:38). The words are nearly the same in both books. Yahuah (God) Almighty says through Esdras, your house is desolate; Yahusha (Jesus) says in the temple, behold, your house is left unto you desolate, and walks out of it. Jeremiah had said it of the first house before Babylon burned it, and Ezekiel watched the glory leave it. Now the one whose glory it was leaves the second house on his own feet, and the house was desolate from that hour whatever the priests kept doing in it. The leadership that killed the prophets lost the house; the children the hen would have gathered are still being gathered.
member_note: 2 Esdras 1:33 — *Thus says the Almighty Yahuah (God), Your house is desolate.* The King said it in the temple and walked out: your house is left unto you desolate (Matthew 23:38).

new_note: *Remember your children that sleep, for I shall bring them out of the sides of the earth, and shew mercy to them: for I am merciful, says Yahuah (God) Almighty.* (2 Esdras 2:31). *For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.* (Luke 15:24). Yahuah (God) tells the mother to remember her children that sleep, because he will bring them out of the sides of the earth and show them mercy. The father in the parable says of his returned son, this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. The son came out of a far country, and the children in 2 Esdras come out of the sides of the earth, and in both the mercy belongs to the father and the merriment follows the return. The ones who sleep are brought out because he is merciful; that is the resurrection hope, and the prodigal's homecoming is a picture of it, the lost child of the house gathered home and counted alive.
member_note: 2 Esdras 2:31 — *Remember your children that sleep, for I shall bring them out of the sides of the earth.* The son who was dead and is alive again (Luke 15:24) is that mercy in a parable.

new_note: *Arise up and stand, behold the number of those that be sealed in the feast of Yahuah (God);* (2 Esdras 2:38). *Go ye therefore into the highways, and as many as ye shall find, bid to the marriage.* (Matthew 22:9). Esdras is told to stand and look at the number of those sealed in the feast of Yahuah (God). In the parable the first guests would not come, so the king sends his servants into the highways to bid as many as they find to the marriage. The ones found on the highways are not strangers to the king; they are the scattered children whose number he already knows, sealed before the servants ever went out. The feast of Yahuah (God) in 2 Esdras and the marriage in Matthew are the same table, and the guests are gathered in from wherever they were scattered.
member_note: 2 Esdras 2:38 — *behold the number of those that be sealed in the feast of Yahuah (God).* The servants sent into the highways gather them to the marriage (Matthew 22:9).

new_note: *I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised Yahuah (God) with songs.* (2 Esdras 2:42). *So those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guests.* (Matthew 22:10). Esdras sees on mount Sion a great people he could not number, all praising Yahuah (God) with songs. The parable ends with the wedding furnished with guests, gathered from the highways, both bad and good. John saw the same crowd in Revelation 7, a great multitude no man could number, out of all nations. Esdras saw the gathered on the mountain, the parable shows the gathering on the roads, and the next verse in each shows the King coming among them to see who is wearing what.
member_note: 2 Esdras 2:42 — *a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised Yahuah (God) with songs.* The wedding furnished with guests (Matthew 22:10) is the same gathered crowd.

new_note: *And in the midst of them there was a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest, and upon every one of their heads he set crowns, and was more exalted; which I marvelled at greatly.* (2 Esdras 2:43). *And when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man which had not on a wedding garment:* (Matthew 22:11). In the midst of the gathered crowd on mount Sion a young man taller than all the rest sets a crown on every head, and the angel tells Esdras a few verses on that this is the Son of Elohim (God) whom they confessed in the world. In the parable the king comes in to see the guests and finds a man with no wedding garment. Both scenes have the King walking among the gathered, and in both what he does depends on what they are wearing; in 2 Esdras the verses before say the gathered have received glorious garments, and these receive crowns. The man without the garment at the marriage receives nothing and is put out. The garment is the righteousness of the saints, and the King himself inspects it.
member_note: 2 Esdras 2:43 — *upon every one of their heads he set crowns, and was more exalted.* The king came in to see the guests and found one without a wedding garment (Matthew 22:11).

new_note: *For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him.* (2 Esdras 3:21). *But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way.* (Matthew 13:25). Esdras says the first Adam bore a wicked heart, transgressed, and was overcome, and so are all who are born of him. The parable says that while men slept an enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat. These are two different facts about one field. The sons of Adam carry the wicked heart, and the law was given to bring fruit out of them in spite of it; the tares are another seed, planted by an enemy, not born of Adam at all. The wheat is wounded, the tares are not wheat, and the harvest will tell them apart.
member_note: 2 Esdras 3:21 — *the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome.* The field of Adam's sons is where the enemy sowed tares while men slept (Matthew 13:25).
flag: Kept the old note's line between the wicked heart inherited by Adam's sons (the wheat) and the tares the enemy sowed (a different seed); wrote it plainly so the two are not collapsed.

new_note: *For the grain of evil seed has been sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning, and how much ungodliness has it brought up to this time? and how much shall it yet bring forth until the time of threshing come?* (2 Esdras 4:30). *Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field:* (Matthew 13:24). Uriel says a grain of evil seed was sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning, that it has brought up ungodliness ever since, and that it will go on bearing until the time of threshing. Yahusha (Jesus) opens his parable with a man sowing good seed in his field, and the verses that follow tell of the enemy's seed and the harvest when the two are separated. Esdras and the King both speak of seed, of two kinds of seed in one ground, and of a threshing that ends the matter. The evil seed is not the last word in either book; the threshing is.
member_note: 2 Esdras 4:30 — *the grain of evil seed has been sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning.* The parable of the good seed sown in the field (Matthew 13:24) runs to the same threshing.

new_note: *For the grain of evil seed has been sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning, and how much ungodliness has it brought up to this time? and how much shall it yet bring forth until the time of threshing come?* (2 Esdras 4:30). *And these are they by the way side, where the word is sown; but when they have heard, Satan cometh immediately, and taketh away the word that was sown in their hearts.* (Mark 4:15). The evil seed in the heart of Adam has been bearing ungodliness since the beginning, Uriel says, and will until the threshing. In the parable of the sower the word is sown and Satan comes at once and takes it out of the heart before it can root. The heart is the ground in both; in one the evil seed is sown into it, in the other the good seed is stolen out of it. Mark's four soils are the field Esdras was shown, and the adversary works the same ground the same way until the harvest.
member_note: 2 Esdras 4:30 — *how much ungodliness has it brought up to this time?.* The same heart is the ground where Satan takes away the word that was sown (Mark 4:15).

new_note: *Then I answered and said, How, and when shall these things come to pass? wherefore are our years few and evil?* (2 Esdras 4:33). *And said unto him, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another?* (Matthew 11:3). Esdras, shown the end and the threshing, asks the question anyone in distress asks: how, and when, and why are our years few and evil. John, in Herod's prison, sends to ask Yahusha (Jesus), art thou he that should come, or do we look for another. John had preached the axe at the root and the fan in the hand, and the fire had not fallen while he sat in chains. Neither question is unbelief. Both are the faithful asking the one who knows the times why the times are not yet what he said they would be.
member_note: 2 Esdras 4:33 — *How, and when shall these things come to pass? wherefore are our years few and evil?.* John's question from prison (Matthew 11:3) is the same question from the same distress.

new_note: *And he answered me, saying, Do not you hasten above the most Highest: for your haste is in vain to be above him, for you have much exceeded.* (2 Esdras 4:34). *And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.* (Matthew 11:6). The angel's answer to Esdras is not a date; it is, do not hasten above the Most High, the times are his and your hurry cannot move them. The King's answer to John is not a date either; after naming the works being done he adds, blessed is he who is not offended in me. Both answers ask the same thing of the one waiting: that he not stumble over the gap between what was promised and what he can see from where he sits. The blessing is on the one who trusts the timing of Yahuah (God) when the timing is the hardest part.
member_note: 2 Esdras 4:34 — *Do not you hasten above the most Highest: for your haste is in vain to be above him.* Blessed is he who is not offended in the waiting (Matthew 11:6).

new_note: *Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers, saying, How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the floor of our reward?* (2 Esdras 4:35). *Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few;* (Matthew 9:37). The souls of the righteous in their chambers ask how long, and when comes the fruit of the floor, the threshing floor where the reward is given. The King looks out over the multitudes and says the harvest is plenteous and the labourers few. Both speak of one harvest. The souls are asking when the floor will be filled; the King is sending men into the field to fill it, and the next verse in 2 Esdras gives the answer the souls received, when the number of seeds is filled. The waiting dead and the working living are looking toward the same floor from opposite sides of it.
member_note: 2 Esdras 4:35 — *How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the floor of our reward?.* The living are sent into the harvest the sleeping righteous wait for (Matthew 9:37).
flag: Old note said the harvest the souls asked about 'is now plenteous' at the King's arrival. The floor of reward in 2 Esdras is the threshing at the end, not Galilee, so I wrote the field being gathered toward that floor rather than the floor having come.

new_note: *Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers, saying, How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the floor of our reward?* (2 Esdras 4:35). *And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.* (Matthew 11:6). The righteous dead ask from their chambers how long they must hope this way. John saw the same souls under the altar asking how long, O Yahuah (Lord), and they were told to rest a little while longer (Revelation 6:9–11). The King's word to John the Baptist in his prison is the word for everyone who waits: blessed is he who is not offended in me. The dead wait in their chambers, the living wait in their chains, and the blessing is on both for not letting the length of the wait turn into offense at the one who set its length.
member_note: 2 Esdras 4:35 — *Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers.* The one who waits without being offended is blessed (Matthew 11:6).

new_note: *Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers, saying, How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the floor of our reward?* (2 Esdras 4:35). *And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.* (Matthew 16:18). The righteous dead are in chambers, Esdras is told, asking when the floor of their reward will come. They are not in torment and they are not in heaven; they are resting and waiting, and later in the book the chambers deliver up the souls committed to them at the resurrection (2 Esdras 7:32). That is what the King means when he says the gates of hell shall not prevail against his assembly. Sheol is a holding place with gates, and the gates do not hold his people past the day he calls them out. The chambers keep the righteous; they do not keep them forever.
member_note: 2 Esdras 4:35 — *the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers.* The chambers hold the righteous until the resurrection; the gates of hell shall not prevail (Matthew 16:18).

new_note: *And to these things Uriel the archangel gave them answer, and said, Even when the number of seeds is filled in you: for he has weighed the world in the balance.* (2 Esdras 4:36). *Pray ye therefore Yahuah (Lord) of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.* (Matthew 9:38). Uriel's answer to the waiting souls is a number: the harvest comes when the number of seeds is filled, and he has weighed the world in the balance. The King's answer to a plenteous harvest with few labourers is a prayer: ask Yahuah (Lord) of the harvest to send forth labourers. The number is his and the timing is his, but the gathering is done by hands he sends, and the labourers he sends are how the seeds are filled up to the number. Esdras was shown why the end waits; the disciples were told what to do while it does.
member_note: 2 Esdras 4:36 — *Even when the number of seeds is filled in you: for he has weighed the world in the balance.* The labourers sent into the harvest (Matthew 9:38) are how the number is filled.

new_note: *Nevertheless as concerning the tokens, behold, the days shall come, that they which dwell upon earth shall be taken in a great number, and the way of truth shall be hidden, and the land shall be barren of faith.* (2 Esdras 5:1). *And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.* (Matthew 24:10). The first sign Esdras is given of the end is not war or famine but this: the way of truth hidden and the land barren of faith. The King gives the same sign in the same order in Matthew 24, many offended, betraying one another, hating one another, and two verses on, because lawlessness abounds the love of many grows cold. Faith does not die by itself; it dies when the way of truth, which is the law of Yahuah (God), is hidden from the people, and lawlessness fills the place it left. Esdras saw the land barren; the King explains what made it so.
member_note: 2 Esdras 5:1 — *the way of truth shall be hidden, and the land shall be barren of faith.* The same sign: many offended, betraying and hating one another (Matthew 24:10).

new_note: *But if the Most High grant you to live, you shall see after the third trumpet that the sun shall suddenly shine again in the night, and the moon thrice in the day:* (2 Esdras 5:4). *Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:* (Matthew 24:29). Esdras is told that those who live to see it will see the sun shine in the night and the moon by day, after the third trumpet. The King says that immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give her light, and the stars will fall. The prophets had said the same of the day of Yahuah (LORD): Isaiah, Joel, Amos, Zephaniah. In both books the disordered heavens come after the trouble, not before it, and in both they are seen by people still standing on the earth. A teaching that has his people carried away before those days has to set 2 Esdras 5 and Matthew 24 both aside to stand.
member_note: 2 Esdras 5:4 — *the sun shall suddenly shine again in the night, and the moon thrice in the day.* The signs in the heavens come after the tribulation of those days (Matthew 24:29).

new_note: *And salt waters shall be found in the sweet, and all friends shall destroy one another; then shall wit hide itself, and understanding withdraw itself into his secret chamber, And shall be sought of many, and yet not be found: then shall unrighteousness and incontinency be multiplied upon earth.* (2 Esdras 5:9–10). *He answered and said unto them, Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.* (Matthew 13:11). Esdras is shown a day when understanding withdraws into its secret chamber and is sought by many and not found. The King tells his disciples why he speaks in parables: to you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom, to them it is not given. Understanding does not vanish from the earth; it withdraws from those who would not have it and is given to those who hear. The many who seek and do not find in Esdras are the ones who, in Matthew, hear and do not understand, because what is withdrawn from one is a gift to the other, and the hearing reveals which is which.
member_note: 2 Esdras 5:9 — *then shall wit hide itself, and understanding withdraw itself into his secret chamber.* To some it is given to know the mysteries; to others it is not (Matthew 13:11).

new_note: *And salt waters shall be found in the sweet, and all friends shall destroy one another; then shall wit hide itself, and understanding withdraw itself into his secret chamber,* (2 Esdras 5:9). *And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.* (Matthew 24:10). Among the signs Esdras is given is that all friends shall destroy one another. The King names the same thing among his: many shall be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another. The pressure of the last days does not only come from outside; it turns friend on friend and brother on brother inside the house, and Paul tasted it when Demas forsook him and no man stood with him at his first answer. Esdras and Matthew both put the betrayal of friends on the list of signs, so the reader will not mistake it for proof that the way was wrong.
member_note: 2 Esdras 5:9 — *all friends shall destroy one another.* Many shall betray one another, and shall hate one another (Matthew 24:10).
